ca_summit_area_the.blurb: The top of Mount Woodson above Poway, where the summit road makes its last switchbacks and a scatter of boulders and short faces sits beside it. Climbing here is a mix of top-rope, crack-focused trad, a little sport and plenty of bouldering, with most roped grades falling in the 5.10s and low 5.11s. The Sail, Crucible and Ogre are the better-known leads and top-ropes, and Renaissance Man is the boulder problem people talk about. Everything sits close to the road, so days are short on approach and easy to combine with a stroll to the summit.

ca_psom_slab.blurb: A big slab high in Pine Creek Canyon, at roughly 7,100 feet, known for long multi-pitch trad climbing with bolted sections mixed in. Routes run from four to seven pitches, and most grades land between 5.8 and 5.10, so it suits parties comfortable on friction and thin cracks. John Fischer Memorial Route, The Big Deal and PBR Street Gang are the lines climbers seek out. Plan on a double rack, a few quickdraws and a good grasp of multi-pitch rappelling for the descent, and expect a cool, quiet day above the canyon floor.
ca_psom_slab.parking_note: Drive up Pine Creek Road from the Highway 395 turnoff. Pull into the dirt area under a grove of trees a little beyond the Scheelite Wall pullout, about seven miles up the canyon road.
ca_psom_slab.approach: A faint but followable path leaves the pullout toward the lower left side of the slab, then bends up and right into the gully below the buttress.

ca_ghetto_wall.blurb: The steepest wall in Malibu Creek State Park, where bolted lines work up through caves and pockets in volcanic rock. This is the park's hard-sport headquarters: grades cluster from 5.11 through 5.13, with a handful of 5.14s and just a couple of 5.9s to warm up on. Ghetto Blaster, Urban Struggle and Ground Zero are among the lines people come for. The wall stays shaded through the morning and early afternoon, which helps in warm weather. The walk in crosses the creek and passes the rock pool, and the deep pockets stay damp for days after rain.
ca_ghetto_wall.approach: From the Planet of the Apes Wall, keep heading west, cross the creek at the easiest spot, scramble through boulders into the back canyon and skirt the rock pool on the traverse.

ca_echo_cove_south_face.blurb: The south side of Echo Cove, one of the busiest corners of Joshua Tree. Short to medium monzogranite routes, mostly traditional with a few top-ropes, run from easy 5.7s up to the low 5.12s, with the bulk in the 5.9 to 5.11 range. Bases are flat and the walls are close to the parking, so it is a popular place for beginners learning to place gear and for groups setting up top-ropes. The face holds shade for much of the day, a plus in warm weather and a chill in midwinter. Expect company.
ca_echo_cove_south_face.parking_note: Take the gravel road signed for Key's Ranch off Big Horn Pass Road and follow it about a quarter mile. A small fenced lot sits at the mouth of the cove; a larger one lies roughly 150 yards back if it is full.

ca_east_face_7.blurb: The east side of Sugarloaf, a tall granite spire rising above the Highway 50 corridor near Kyburz. Mostly crack-based trad with some bolted lines, the climbing is steep and sustained, with grades concentrated from 5.10 to 5.12 and a few harder tests. Grand Illusion, Telesis and Bird Man are the headline routes, and Farley, Nearly and Crushed Velvet give a taste at lower grades. At roughly 4,000 feet it climbs well in cool seasons, but summer days can be very hot. The hike up is steep and takes about half an hour.
ca_east_face_7.parking_note: Use the dirt pullout on the south side of Highway 50 past School Road, about halfway to Larch Lane, and cross the highway on foot to find the climbers' trail.

ca_the_secret_passage.blurb: A narrow slot canyon within Monkeyface Falls in the San Bernardino Mountains, offering sport climbing in a cool, shaded setting with waterfalls nearby. Nearly every route is bolted, and the grades pile up in the 5.9 and 5.10 range, with some 5.11s and 5.12s for variety. Positive Reinforcement, Negative Reinforcement and Baja Blast are good places to start. It is a popular escape on hot days thanks to the trees and shade. The way into the canyon includes a short talus hike and some scrambling, and rappelling knowledge is useful.
ca_the_secret_passage.parking_note: Follow Valley of the Falls Drive off Highway 38, continuing straight where the main road bends toward Frustration Creek. A dirt pull-off sits on the right roughly a quarter mile along.

ca_p_wall.blurb: The tallest wall on Bishop Peak, an old volcanic plug above San Luis Obispo, recognizable by the painted P on its face. The dacite here gives vertical face climbing and cracks, mostly traditional with a handful of bolted lines, and grades gather around 5.9 and 5.10. Epidural, P-Crack and Senior Moment are good places to start. Summers run hot here, so late fall through early spring is the comfortable window. The path in is steep, with loose rock near the base.
ca_p_wall.parking_note: Park on the street at the cul-de-sac at the end of Highland Drive, west of Santa Rosa Street. The marked trail to the peak begins here.
ca_p_wall.approach: Follow the main trail up almost to the trees, then angle right and loop back left through the brush; the final stretch is steep with loose rock.

ca_old_camp_bluff.blurb: A granite bluff high above Silver Lake, off Highway 88 near Kirkwood. Clean cracks and bolted faces share the wall, and the routes mostly span 5.7 to 5.12 with plenty in the 5.9 to 5.11 range. Old Camp Dihedral, Meat Lover Crack AKA Bat Crack, Dragon's Back and Wile E. Crack show the range. The base sits in tree shade while the wall itself catches sun from morning into early afternoon. Because the altitude keeps it cooler than the foothill crags, it suits summer days. Top-rope anchors need your own hardware.
ca_old_camp_bluff.parking_note: Pull off along Highway 88 near Silver Lake, using roadside space near either of the gates.
ca_old_camp_bluff.approach: A trail marked by cairns passes the gate and heads to the top of the wall; walk down the back or around the left side to reach the base. Expect a short hike.

ca_mt_gorgeous.blurb: One of the most popular walls in Malibu Creek State Park and home to some of its longest sport routes, all bolted and climbing pocketed volcanic rock. Grades run from the 5.6s up past 5.12, with most between 5.10 and 5.12, so it works for newer leaders and strong ones. Feel The Bern, Marauding Monkeys and Simon Says are among the favorites. The wall faces west, so the base is shaded in the morning and well into the day by trees, with sun arriving mid-afternoon. Bees and wasps sometimes nest in the pockets, and a rack of around sixteen draws covers most lines.
